sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast. My name is Emily and I am so happy you are here
today. In this episode, we will travel to Tashkent, the capital city of Uzbekistan.
Tashkent is a place where the old and the new come together. It has colorful markets,
green parks, modern buildings, and deep history. Let's explore this amazing city together,
in slow and simple English. Are you ready? Let's begin. Part 1. Where is Tashkent?
Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia
between Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, and Turkmenistan. Tashkent is in
the northeast part of the country, near the border with Kazakhstan. It is the largest city in Central
Asia, with more than 2.5 million people. Tashkent is a very important city. It is the heart of
Uzbekistan's politics, economy, and culture. Part 2. A short history. Tashkent is one of the
oldest cities in Central Asia. Its history goes back more than 2000 years. Long ago, it was called
Chach and later Shash. Because it was on the Silk Road, it became a busy trade center.
Merchants from China, Persia, India, and Europe passed through Tashkent. Over time,
many different empires ruled the city. The Persians, Turks, Mongols, and Russians.
In the 19th century, Tashkent became part of the Russian Empire. Later, it was the capital of the
Uzbek-Soviet Socialist Republic during the time of the Soviet Union. After Uzbekistan became
independent in 1991, Tashkent became the capital of the new country. Today, Tashkent is a mix of
ancient culture and modern life. Full of energy, color, and movement.
Part 3. Tashkent has a continental climate. This means hot summers and cold winters.
In summer, the weather is usually very warm, around 35 to 40 degrees celsius.
People enjoy drinking cold tea and eating ice cream outside. In winter, it can be quite cold,
sometimes below zero Greek cells. But it is also sunny on many days, even in winter.
Spring and autumn are beautiful seasons. The air is fresh and the trees are full of color.
Part 4. What you can see in Tashkent. Tashkent has many interesting places to visit.
Let's explore some of them together. The Amir Tumor Square. This is the main square in the center of
Tashkent. It has a big statue of Amir Tumor, a famous Uzbek leader from the 14th century.
The square is surrounded by green parks, fountains, and important buildings.
The Kukkal Dash Madrasa. This beautiful Islamic school was built in the 16th century.
It is one of the oldest buildings in the city. The Madrasa has blue tiles and peaceful courtyards.
It shows the traditional Islamic architecture of Central Asia. The Hazrati Imam Complex.
This is the spiritual center of Tashkent. It has mosques, libraries, and the famous Quran of
Kaylith Uthman, one of the oldest Quran in the world. Many visitors come here to learn about the
history and faith of Uzbekistan. Chorsubazar. Chorsubazar is the heart of daily life in Tashkent.
It is a large colorful market where people buy fruits, vegetables, spices, and clothes.
The smell of bread and spices fills the air. You can see people smiling, talking, and bargaining.
It's a great place to feel the local culture. The Metro of Tashkent. Tashkent has one of the most
beautiful metro systems in the world. Each station is like a work of art with marble,
chandeliers, and mosaics. It was built during the Soviet period and is still clean and efficient.
The TV Tower. The Tashkent TV Tower is one of the tallest towers in Central Asia.
It is 375 meters tall. You can go up to the observation deck and see all of Tashkent from above.
Part 5. Culture and People. People in Tashkent are known for their hospitality. They are warm,
kind, and always ready to help visitors. Family is very important in Uzbek culture.
People like to spend time together, especially during meals. They also celebrate many traditional
festivals, such as Navruz, the Spring Festival. The main language is Uzbek, but many people also
speak Russian and some English. Traditional clothes, like the Delpa, a small cap, and colorful dresses,
are sometimes worn during festivals. Music and dance are also important. You can hear
traditional Uzbek instruments like the dutar and tambour and see dances full of energy and joy.
Part 6. Food in Tashkent. Uzbek food is rich and delicious. Meals are full of flavor, meat,
rice, and fresh vegetables. Plav Plav is the national dish of Uzbekistan. It's made with rice,
carrots, onions, and meat, usually lamb or beef. Every region has its own special recipe.
In Tashkent, Plav is cooked in large pots and served with tea and salads.
Samsa samsa is a baked pastry filled with meat, onions, or pumpkin. It's crispy on the outside and
soft inside. You can find samsa everywhere, in bakeries, markets, and on the street.
Lagman. Lagman is a noodle soup with meat and vegetables. It's warm, spicy, and full of color.
Non-non is traditional Uzbek bread. It's round and baked in a clay oven called a tandir.
It smells wonderful and is eaten with almost every meal. And of course, tea. Green tea is the most
popular drink. It is served in small cups called peala, often with sweets and dried fruits.
Part 7. Modern Tashkent today. Tashkent is a very modern and growing city. There are tall buildings,
big shopping malls, and international restaurants. At the same time, there are also quiet streets,
gardens, and traditional houses. The city has wide roads, modern transport, and many parks full
of trees and flowers. Young people in Tashkent love technology, music, and fashion.
They study in universities, work in cafes, and enjoy life in this lively capital.
Part 8. Festivals and Traditions. The most important festival in Tashkent is Navruz,
the celebration of spring and the new year. It happens on March 21st. People clean their homes,
visit friends, and cook special foods like Sumalak, made from wheat sprouts.
During Navruz, the city is full of music, dance, and smiles. People wear colorful clothes and
children play outside. There are also many concerts, art shows, and national holidays where people
celebrate their culture and history. Part 9. Language Practice. Simple English Sentences.
Let's review what we learned today in slow and easy English. Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan.
It is in Central Asia. It is a very old city with a long history. People speak Uzbek and Russian.
Plav is a traditional food. The weather is hot in summer and cold in winter. You can visit the
Chorsu Bazaar. People are kind and friendly. Tashkent is modern and beautiful.
Very good. You are learning a lot. Part 10. Why visit Tashkent?
Tashkent is not as famous as some other capitals, but it is very special. It is clean, safe, and full
of culture. You can walk through history, taste amazing food, and meet kind people.
You can visit ancient mosques in the morning and modern art galleries in the afternoon.
You can listen to traditional music or go to a new coffee shop. Tashkent is a bridge between the
east and the west, between the past and the future. If you love history, architecture, and food,
you will love Tashkent. Part 11. So my friends, today we visited Tashkent,
the capital of Uzbekistan. We learned about its long history, its beautiful markets,
its kind people, and its delicious food. Tashkent is a city where old traditions and modern life
live side by side. It is a place full of warmth, music, and colors. Thank you for joining me on
this journey. I hope you enjoyed learning English with me while exploring a new part of the world.
keep learning, keep smiling, and keep discovering the world in slow English. Goodbye.
